comments.content: The REPL instances created in `getReplOutput` are never closed. Consider capturing the return value of `repl.start(...)` and closing it (e.g. `r.close()`) after collecting output to avoid leaking REPL/readline instances across the many `it` blocks that use this helper.

`outputStream.write` is reassigned only after `inputStream.emit('data', input)` would be able to produce output, but note that writes triggered synchronously during `repl.start` (e.g. the initial prompt) are lost because the override happens after `repl.start`. Confirm this ordering is intended; if the prompt should be captured, move the `outputStream.write` override before `repl.start`.

This test relies on `repl.start` using default input/output (stdin/stdout) since no streams are provided. This attaches to the real stdin and may interfere with the test runner or leave the process listening on stdin. Consider passing explicit `input`/`output` ArrayStreams here as well, consistent with `getReplOutput`.
